name: Soviet patriotism
summary: Soviet patriotism is loyalty to the USSR as the homeland of socialism, joining Marxist-Leninist commitments (planned economy, party leadership, strong socialist state) with pride in the Soviet and, especially in its Stalin-era form, Russian past. It holds the Soviet people to be a multinational community bound by the friendship of peoples, with Russians as the leading nation, and treats defence of the homeland as a socialist duty.
scope: The Stalin-era form (about 1934 to 1953), based on Stalin's 1939 Congress report, his 1941 war speeches and 1945 toast, and the scholarly description of the doctrine. It excludes later Khrushchev-to-Gorbachev versions of the supranational Soviet people and modern Russian nostalgic revivals; it also differs from Lenin's earlier proletarian internationalism. Because the sources are speeches and not a systematic programme, many answers on topics they do not address are inferred and low confidence.

keyFigures.name: Joseph Stalin
keyFigures.role: Soviet leader who made Soviet patriotism state policy and gave the wartime speeches.

keyFigures.name: Vladimir Lenin
keyFigures.role: Founder of the Soviet state who separated proletarian patriotism from bourgeois nationalism.

sources.title: Report on the Work of the Central Committee to the Eighteenth Congress of the CPSU(B.) (10 March 1939)
sources.author: J. V. Stalin
sources.usedFor: The state under capitalist encirclement, socialism in one country, the party, the Soviet intelligentsia, friendship of the nations and the task of cultivating Soviet patriotism.

sources.title: Radio Broadcast (3 July 1941)
sources.author: J. V. Stalin
sources.usedFor: The patriotic war of liberation, rallying around the Party, discipline and tribunals, scorched earth, collective farms and alliance with Britain and the US.

sources.title: Speech at the Red Square parade (7 November 1941)
sources.author: J. V. Stalin
sources.usedFor: Invocation of Russian ancestors, Lenin's banner, the 1918 intervention war and the condemnation of Hitlerite Germany.

sources.title: Toast to the Russian People (24 May 1945)
sources.author: J. V. Stalin
sources.usedFor: The Russian people as leading force among the Soviet peoples and the people's confidence in the government.

sources.usedFor: The friendship of peoples doctrine, the Russians as elder brother and the deportations.

universal-healthcare.rationale: A socialist state that claims to serve the whole working population is expected to provide health care as a public service, as Soviet practice did.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Not discussed; wages were state-set under planning, so a worker-friendly state would favour raising the lowest pay.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Stalin's 1939 report presents the planned socialist economy as superior to capitalism; markets are the system being replaced.

public-ownership.rationale: Socialist public ownership of industry is the economic base the 1939 report says has been built in the USSR.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: The exploiting classes were abolished, so the question was moot; an adherent would back soaking the rich on principle.

unions-good.rationale: Soviet unions were state-aligned bodies serving production and the party; adherents would call them good but not independent.

property-fundamental.rationale: Property in means of production was abolished as socialism's base; only personal property is protected, and it yields to the state.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Private corporations did not exist; the logic of state control would favour tight regulation of any that did.

cut-welfare.rationale: Social provision for workers is part of the socialist claim to care for people; cutting it would be rejected.

worker-ownership.rationale: Ownership by the working people through the socialist state and collective farms is the model, though not syndicalist worker control.

surveillance-ok.rationale: The state needs strong intelligence and punitive organs against encirclement, per Stalin's 1939 report, so security surveillance is accepted.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Not addressed; the disciplined, productivist Soviet moral order makes recreational drug legalization alien.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Not addressed directly; the state condemned chauvinism and national hatred and enforced the friendship of peoples line.

strong-leader.rationale: Stalin asks the people to rally round the Party of Lenin and Stalin; a strong leader is accepted, though the party is nominally central.

state-harmful.rationale: Stalin explicitly rejects the state withering away while encirclement lasts, defending a strong state, army and security organs.

limit-guns.rationale: Not addressed; a state monopoly on force suggests strict civilian limits.

empower-police-military.rationale: The 1939 report insists on a strong army, punitive organs and intelligence service as long as capitalist encirclement lasts.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Not addressed; Soviet doctrine treated prostitution as a capitalist survival to be abolished.

decide-locally.rationale: Stalinist Soviet patriotism was centralist, built on a single Soviet people under central leadership.

rehabilitation.rationale: Soviet penal theory spoke of re-education, though practice was harsh; inferred and contested.

traditional-family.rationale: Not in the sources read; inferred from the Stalin-era turn to a stable, pronatalist family and conservative social order.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Not addressed; the Stalin-era state criminalized homosexuality and gave this no place.

abortion-legal.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; the Stalin-era state restricted abortion from 1936, but later Soviet patriotism legalized it, so contested.

more-religion-public.rationale: The wartime alliance with the Orthodox Church was a tactical concession, while the state stayed officially atheist.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: The friendship of peoples line rejected national and racial oppression, but this was framed as already achieved in the USSR.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Not addressed; Soviet doctrine stressed equality of women in work, but Stalin-era orthodoxy was not constructionist.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Stalin's 1941 speech invokes Russian ancestors Nevsky, Donskoy and Suvorov; patriotism embraced national heroes and traditions.

gradual-change.rationale: The ideology came from revolution and rapid industrialization; established pre-revolutionary institutions were not respected.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Not addressed; a closed, controlled-border state would favour restricted movement.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Stalin stresses Soviet state strength under encirclement, not supranational authority; the UN postdates most texts.

free-trade.rationale: The planned economy relied on state control of foreign trade; the 1939 report treats capitalist economies as the rival system.

nation-first.rationale: Patriotism puts defence of the Soviet homeland first, but the USSR also saw itself as leading world socialism.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Stalin's wartime speeches justify war as defense and liberation, not human-rights intervention; inferred.

open-borders.rationale: Not addressed; a state that must be strong against encirclement would not open its borders.

limit-growth.rationale: Stalin's 1939 report celebrates growth of Soviet industry and output; no concern for ecological limits.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Anachronistic; the sources contain no basis to place it.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Soviet doctrine prized industrial and scientific progress, which the 1939 report treats as the base of socialist prosperity.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the Soviet commitment to technology, industry and military strength.

revolution-justified.rationale: Stalin presents the 1917 revolution and the 1918 war against interventionists as the foundation of the Soviet state under Lenin's banner.

experts-over-public.rationale: The 1939 report praises the Soviet intelligentsia but under party leadership, so experts serve rather than rule.

central-planning.rationale: The planned socialist economy is the 1939 report's central achievement and the basis for its claims over capitalism.

socialized-markets.rationale: Stalinist doctrine treated planned allocation as the socialist norm and markets as residual.

land-value-tax.rationale: Not addressed; a land-nationalizing planned economy has no use for such a tax.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Not addressed; inheritance of productive property was abolished, so heavy taxation of large inheritances fits the logic.

basic-income.rationale: Socialism is distribution according to work; an unconditional income would contradict that principle.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: The state monopoly of foreign trade protected Soviet industry; inferred as a policy of economic independence.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Directing investment to heavy industry and strategic sectors was the core of Soviet planning.

widespread-small-property.rationale: The ideology collectivizes agriculture and nationalizes industry rather than spreading small private ownership.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Not addressed; the state banking system is part of the planned economy.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: The state, not bodies of employers and workers, set wages and prices; class collaboration was rejected.

one-party-rule.rationale: Stalin calls on the people to rally around the Party of Lenin and Stalin, which guides the state.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Soviet patriotism honoured Russian heroes but defined the state against the old regime and Tsarist rule.

democracy-best.rationale: Soviet doctrine claimed socialist democracy as the highest form, but it rejected competitive multi-party democracy.

direct-votes.rationale: Not addressed; decisions were taken by party and state organs, not by referendum.

workers-councils.rationale: The soviets were the nominal basis of state power, though real authority lay with the party.

right-to-secede.rationale: Lenin backed national self-determination and Soviet republics had formal secession rights, but this was not practiced.

natural-rulers.rationale: Rule belonged to the party as vanguard, justified by ideology and not by innate merit.

political-violence-never.rationale: Stalin presents war, discipline and tribunals as justified by the revolution and defense of the homeland.

war-builds-character.rationale: Stalin calls the war a necessary defense, not an ennobling good; inferred.

separate-church-state.rationale: The state stayed officially atheist and separate from religion, despite the wartime accommodation with the Orthodox Church.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Soviet law was secular; the Church alliance was tactical and gave it no legal role.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Stalin stresses the state's army, punitive organs and security services; private provision is contrary to this.

military-superiority.rationale: The 1939 report insists on a strong Red Army and Navy for as long as capitalist encirclement lasts.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The Soviet people was a multinational community, with the friendship of peoples as its principle.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Marxist-Leninist premise: the Soviet state and its patriotism rest on the revolution against exploiting classes.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Stalin-era doctrine paid by work under socialism and attacked wage levelling; equality means abolishing exploiter classes.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: The nationalities policy gave republics and autonomous units, not general indigenous authority over land.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Soviet doctrine condemned colonialism; reparations were not a developed theme, so inferred.

civilizational-union.rationale: Unity was on the basis of socialism and the Soviet people, not of religion or civilization.

self-interest-moral.rationale: The ideology stresses collective, socialist morality and duty to the Soviet homeland.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Stalin's 1941 speech demands sacrifice, discipline and duty to the homeland above individual interest.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Not addressed; Soviet doctrine valued nature for use in building socialism.

limit-population.rationale: Not addressed; Stalin-era policy was pronatalist.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: The 1939 report celebrates industrialization as the basis of socialism.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Rapid technological and industrial advance was prized, though under state direction rather than disruption.

human-enhancement.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from state-directed priorities and no support for individual enhancement.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Anachronistic; party leadership, not automation, was the decision-maker.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Inferred from the insistence on strong intelligence organs that the state's security cannot be impeded.

restore-past-order.rationale: Soviet patriotism honoured the past but looked forward to building socialism and communism.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Policy is judged by the correct Marxist-Leninist line; pragmatism was subordinate to it.

direct-action.rationale: Change came from a disciplined party-led state, not spontaneous direct action.

means-match-ends.rationale: Leninist doctrine accepts dictatorial and coercive means to build a classless society.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Industrial civilization is the base of socialism in the 1939 report.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Stalin-era doctrine kept specialization; abolition belonged to a distant communism.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Distribution by need is the Marxist-Leninist final goal of communism, with distribution by work under socialism.

production-for-use.rationale: The planned socialist economy is meant to serve social needs rather than profit.

profit-exploitation.rationale: The 1939 report counts the abolition of exploiting classes as the achievement of socialism.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: The Soviet state is described as proletarian power, with its organs turned against enemies.

collective-farming.rationale: Collective farms are the Soviet agricultural form; Stalin's 1941 speech tells collective farmers to hand grain to the state.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Leninist theory of imperialism, and the 1939 report treats capitalist encirclement as the source of danger.

taxation-theft.rationale: The planned state relies on state revenue; the claim is contrary to the doctrine.

harm-principle.rationale: The state may restrict far more than harm, to protect socialism and the unity of Soviet society.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Collective and national rights are part of the doctrine, as in friendship of peoples.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Free emigration was not accepted; the state's authority takes precedence.

state-as-business.rationale: The state serves collective socialist goals and not customers.

positive-liberty.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; Soviet doctrine held that real freedom rests on material security.

media-academia-power.rationale: Media and universities were instruments of the party, so the thesis would be rejected.

hereditarian-race.rationale: The friendship of peoples line rejected racial hierarchy among Soviet peoples.

organic-representation.rationale: Representation via soviets and the party; organic representation is a corporatist idea.

total-state.rationale: The party-state directed economy, education and culture, though Soviet doctrine denied the label.

national-rebirth.rationale: Patriotism drew on past glory, but the framing was defence and building socialism, not rebirth from decadence.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Stalin frames the war as defence and liberation; stated doctrine was not expansionist, though practice diverged.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: The state rests on party and state institutions, not feudal personal oaths.

bound-labor.rationale: Serfdom is the old regime's system; collectivization claimed to free peasants from exploitation.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Marxism-Leninism claims objective science, though ties knowledge to class; inferred.

universal-morality.rationale: Morality is class-based in Marxism-Leninism; inferred.

single-common-good.rationale: The 1939 report describes Soviet society as morally and politically united without antagonistic classes.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Not addressed directly; the ideology favoured assimilation within the multinational Soviet people.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Not addressed; citizenship tied to Soviet territory and state.

revive-national-language.rationale: Not addressed; policy favoured Russian as the common language, with a Soviet people.

workplace-democracy.rationale: One-man management under party direction was Stalin-era practice.

school-vouchers.rationale: Education was a state monopoly; private choice would contradict this.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Not addressed; planning by the state is not bound by budget orthodoxy.

economic-freedom.rationale: Economic freedom in the market sense is the capitalism the Soviet system rejects.

rule-by-example.rationale: Authority rested on party law and discipline, though exemplary conduct was praised.

national-self-determination.rationale: Lenin supported self-determination and non-Russian republics, though the Stalin-era centralism limited it.

force-without-un.rationale: Anachronistic; Soviet defence of the homeland did not wait for outside approval.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Scientific materialism is official, though the wartime Church alliance qualified this.

class-collaboration.rationale: Class struggle, not partnership, is the basis, though Stalin saw the classes within the USSR as no longer hostile.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Stalin invoked Nevsky, Donskoy and Suvorov, so cultural heritage was preserved and used.

dominated-front.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; inferred from the USSR's anti-imperialist stance.

workers-nation.rationale: The friendship of peoples line stresses proletarian internationalism, though patriotism now focuses on the Soviet state.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Soviet doctrine promoted equal public roles for women; Stalin-era family policy was conservative, so low.

ban-interest.rationale: The Soviet banking system paid interest on savings; prohibition was not part of the doctrine.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Friendship of peoples and the multinational Soviet people reject racial segregation.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The 1939 report treats the state as the instrument of class rule, with the Soviet state serving the working people.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the industrial growth priority.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Inferred from the single Soviet people and Russian as common language, but with national forms allowed.

elite-replacement.rationale: The friendship of peoples line treats such conspiracies as chauvinist nonsense.

proportional-representation.rationale: Not addressed; the party-led soviet system does not turn on party proportionality.

national-mission.rationale: The USSR saw itself as the leading socialist country, with Soviet forces liberating Europe's peoples per Stalin.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Soviet doctrine claimed the end of women's oppression in the USSR; inferred.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Eugenic limits conflicted with Soviet doctrine on the primacy of environment.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: The state's security organs are valued and shielded; accountability for killings was not a theme.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Stalin explicitly rejects a minimal state.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: The friendship of peoples line is hostile to racial barriers.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Equality of nations and peoples is stated in friendship of peoples, but the Soviet state also discriminated, so not +2.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Stalin's 1939 report affirms that socialism has been built in the USSR alone and that the state must be strong because of encirclement.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Anti-colonial doctrine suggests acceptance, though not discussed in the sources.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: A single Soviet legal order applied to all citizens, religions disestablished.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Not addressed; the state's atheism did not turn on conversion rules.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Not addressed; irrelevant to the doctrine, which was against religious bans.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Soviet schools were secular and promoted scientific materialism.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Stalin says the state remains, and the army, punitive organs and intelligence service must be strong, while capitalist encirclement lasts.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Stalin's 1945 toast credits the people's confidence in the government, though the doctrine rests on party guidance.

trade-surplus.rationale: Not addressed; the state monopoly of foreign trade was driven by planning needs, not by a surplus doctrine.

population-transfer.rationale: Roughly 6 million people were deported between 1939 and 1953 per Wikipedia, so adherents' state practice accepted it, though not as stated doctrine.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Stalin's justification of revolutionary and wartime force is the opposite of this absolute principle.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: The planned economy substituted socialist emulation for competition; struggle between peoples is rejected.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Opposition parties were banned in the one-party state under Stalin.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Not addressed; closest to the Marxist critique of class domination.

separated-powers.rationale: Soviet doctrine held that power belongs to the soviets and the party, not to checking branches.

vanguard-party.rationale: The Party of Lenin and Stalin leads the people, as in Leninist theory.

priority-to-poor.rationale: The state claims to serve the working people, who are given first priority.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Housing was state-owned; sale into private hands runs against it.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Strikes against the workers' state were not recognized in Stalin-era practice.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Marxist doctrine blames social institutions, not population, for poverty.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: The friendship of peoples line claims multinational unity strengthens society.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Appointment by the party and elections within the soviet system, not lotteries.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Stalin orders military tribunals for deserters and panic-mongers and treats saboteurs as enemies in the 1941 speech.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: The state fixes prices in the planned economy as a normal feature.

party-controls-media.rationale: The party guides the press and propaganda in the Soviet system.

party-commands-army.rationale: Stalin's 1941 speech places the State Committee of Defence and the Party at the head of the war effort.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Not addressed; a controlled-entry state would be restrictive.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Lenin's principle was modest pay for officials, but Stalin-era practice differed.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Democratic centralism binds members to decisions once adopted; the 1939 report praises party discipline and purging.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: The USSR defended its own state sovereignty; it was not part of a pooled union.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Command was by a State Defence Committee and the party, not the head of state alone.

church-by-bishops.rationale: The state was indifferent to church governance; only its alliance with the Orthodox Church touches this.

clerical-rule.rationale: The state was atheist and never gave clerics authority.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Soviet patriotism backs the government in wars of national defence, though Leninist doctrine endorsed defeatism in imperialist wars.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Socialist realism subordinated art to the party's moral and political aims; the sources do not discuss it directly.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: The leader and party were not subject to term limits in Stalin-era practice.

recall-officials.rationale: The soviet system theoretically allowed recall, though it was little used.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Stalin welcomed alliance with Britain and the US in 1941 and the Allies are cited alongside the USSR in November.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Housing was state-owned and allocated; owning for every family was not the aim.

people-in-arms.rationale: The 1939 report insists on a regular Red Army and Navy.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Collectivization and industrial urbanization were central goals.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Inferred from the unification of Ukrainian and Belarusian lands in 1939; not discussed as a principle.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Stalin calls the Soviet intelligentsia of the flesh and blood of the people.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Equality of peoples is official, but Russians were described as the elder brother and first among equals.

death-penalty.rationale: Stalin demands tribunals and the harshest punishment for deserters and saboteurs in wartime.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Not addressed; policy varied between periods, so no confident answer.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Scientific materialism was official; creationism would be rejected.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Not addressed; the state censored morality in culture, so inferred.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: The multinational Soviet people was defined by state belonging, not by descent.

minority-language-support.rationale: Nationalities policy supported national forms, though Russian was promoted as the common language.

religious-exemptions.rationale: The state did not grant exemptions from general laws for religious reasons.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Conformity and moral-political unity were prized.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Not addressed; anti-imperialist doctrine favours cancellation.

constituent-assembly.rationale: The Bolsheviks dissolved the Constituent Assembly under Lenin; the state rests on soviets and the party.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Rapid industrialization under party discipline was the Stalin-era model; not directly stated in the sources.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Not addressed; internationalist doctrine favours assistance, though framed as solidarity.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the demand for military strength and independence.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The head of state was chosen through soviet bodies, not directly.

central-bank-independence.rationale: The state bank is part of the planned economy and subordinate to the plan.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Stalin's wartime call to fight for every inch of land, but not a stated doctrine on peace deals.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Personal property is allowed, subordinate to socialist ownership; the common good limits it.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: The 1939 report says socialism has been built in the USSR; Soviet patriots reject the state-capitalist label.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from priority on industrial development.

collective-defense.rationale: Stalin welcomes Allied support and mutual aid in 1941, but this is not a doctrine statement on alliance clauses.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Soviet practice annexed territories in 1939-40; adherents would reject this view.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Soviet policy kept the church under state control, even in the wartime alliance.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The leader is tied to the party, as in the Party of Lenin and Stalin.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: The centralist Soviet state held its territory together; this was not tested by formal secession.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Soviet republics were to have the same system and national forms but socialist content.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Officially atheist; a divine ruler is contrary to the doctrine, whatever the leader cult.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Not addressed; progressive taxation fits socialism.

character-from-environment.rationale: Marxist-Leninist doctrine holds that character is formed by social conditions, as in the 1939 report on the new Soviet people.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Formally the state is bound by the constitution; though practice was different.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Soviet doctrine rejected mixing of classes in government.

leader-cult.rationale: Stalin was honoured as leader in the Party of Lenin and Stalin, which is the invocation in 1941.

equal-parenting.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; no basis for placing it.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: The 1939 report says exploiting classes were eliminated and Soviet society is united, though Stalin spoke of enemies.

land-redistribution.rationale: Land was taken from landowners and then collectivized, not given to individual farmers permanently.

refugee-return.rationale: Not addressed; policy of deportation conflicts, so no confident answer.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: A secular state would not punish leaving religion.

women-must-cover.rationale: Soviet policy campaigned against veiling as backward.

common-currency.rationale: Not addressed; the ruble was the Soviet state's own currency.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Unity was by the Soviet people, not language families.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Stalin's nationalities policy opposed national cultural autonomy as a substitute for territorial republics, but this is inferred, not read directly.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Soviet doctrine favoured equality within the multinational state, rather than founding homelands.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Historical materialism is the basis of Marxism-Leninism.

ban-cartels.rationale: Not addressed; the state economy was a planned monopoly.

no-bailouts.rationale: Not addressed; the state did not face private-firm failures.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Courts were subordinate to the party and soviet system, but not as a populist majority doctrine.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Not addressed; an official line on women's equality implies support.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Socialism in one country implied economic self-sufficiency, though no colonies existed.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Anachronistic; no basis for placing it.

moral-incentives.rationale: Stalin appeals to sacrifice and duty, though material incentives were kept.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: The Bolshevik revolution is Soviet patriotism's founding event, but Leninist doctrine required mass conditions.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: The 1939 report celebrates the abolition of old privileged classes.

history-own-civilization.rationale: History teaching celebrated the Russian and Soviet past through national heroes.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Soviet doctrine was anti-colonial, but Russians as elder brothers suggests tutelage, so inferred.

patriotic-education.rationale: The 1939 report sets the party the task to develop and cultivate Soviet patriotism.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Not addressed; the nationalities policy promoted non-Russian cadres, but the context is not comparable.

public-money-creation.rationale: The state bank issues currency under the plan.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: The 1939 report portrays capitalism in crisis; Leninist doctrine expected collapse.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Soviet influence over former Tsarist lands was inherited, but not discussed as doctrine.

delink-world-market.rationale: Socialism in one country implied separation from the world market.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Leninist theory of imperialism, though not discussed in the sources.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Equality of peoples is official, so private discrimination is not defended.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Rights were granted by the state, not entrenched against it.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Stalin demands unity and discipline, including tribunals for traitors.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Gramscian; not in the sources, though Marxism-Leninism sees culture as class-based.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Leninist imperialism theory suggests yes, but not discussed in the sources.

party-own-road.rationale: The Soviet party led the world communist movement, so direction from Moscow was normal.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Socialism in one country meant building from own resources.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Not addressed; indigenous leadership was handled by national republics only.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Stalin used Tsarist-era heroes, so such figures are honoured despite their faults.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from emphasis on female emancipation.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Not addressed; no basis for the view.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: The Soviet system presented itself as a distinct path, not Western liberal democracy.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: State social insurance is the socialist model.

single-official-language.rationale: Russian promoted as common language but other languages had official support, so split.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Anachronistic; no basis for the view.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; inferred from the stress on collective ethic.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Soviet support for revolutionary movements; not discussed in the sources.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred only from the later Brezhnev doctrine, not Stalin-era sources.

corporate-influence.rationale: Capitalist corporations hold power in capitalist states per Marxist-Leninist doctrine.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: The state protects itself against encirclement and foreign influence.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Inferred from the Stalin-era family law and bonuses for large families.

residents-only-property.rationale: Not addressed; land was state-owned, so no direct bearing.

job-guarantee.rationale: Guaranteed employment is a central claim of the Soviet system.

democratic-peace.rationale: Leninist theory sees capitalist democracies as imperialist.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Stalin demands discipline and punishment for deserters; duty to the state is central.

non-intervention.rationale: The USSR interpreted its duties as supporting socialist movements elsewhere.

industrial-unions.rationale: Soviet unions were organized by industry, though not discussed.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Friendship of peoples rejects accusations against national minorities in doctrine, though the late Stalin-era campaigns did not.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Stalin-era policy strengthened the legal family.

local-production.rationale: Not addressed; planning is national in scale.

informal-organisation.rationale: The party is a permanent disciplined organization.

national-law-over-international.rationale: State sovereignty emphasized, though not discussed on this point.

religious-nation.rationale: The nation is defined by the Soviet people and socialism, not religion.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Not addressed; the Soviet state held to equal relations of sovereign states in doctrine.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Centralist state, with revenue shared under the plan.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Personal belongings stay private while means of production are held in common, as in the Soviet constitution; not read in the sources, so medium.

defeat-communism.rationale: The Soviet state considered itself the socialist bloc against capitalist encirclement.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Public services were provided directly by the state.

religion-illusion.rationale: Marxist-Leninist doctrine holds this, even when the Church alliance was a wartime expedient.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Classical Marxist view that capitalism created the base for socialism; mentioned in the doctrine, not in the sources.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Marxist-Leninist doctrine ties women's emancipation to socialist economy.

socialized-care.rationale: Early Soviet doctrine called for the socialization of housework; Stalin-era family policy qualified this.

cooperative-communities.rationale: The state and collective farms, not small communities, are the form.

majority-settlement.rationale: Ethnic Russians were encouraged to settle in other republics per Wikipedia.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: The Soviet state claimed to be socialist and building communism.

historical-land-claim.rationale: The "homeland" appeal in 1941 is tied to the Soviet state, not to ancient ties.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Stalin condemned Nazi crimes against peoples.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: The Stalin-era USSR criminalized male homosexuality from 1934; this is not in the sources read.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The 1939 report praises purging the party and identifies enemies; opposition was suppressed.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Anti-colonial in doctrine, though critics call the USSR an empire.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Religious war doctrine is contrary to Soviet secularism.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Soviet doctrine claimed mass participation through soviets and workplaces, though by party direction.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Anachronistic; class is the main category in Marxism-Leninism.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the conservative Stalin-era social line.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: The class struggle is the dividing line.

alienated-labor.rationale: Marxist theory; socialism claims to end exploitation of labour.

islam-incompatible.rationale: The friendship of peoples line rejects such a claim.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: The Soviet state was officially atheist and derived authority from the working people and the party, not from God.

social-market-economy.rationale: The planned economy is the alternative to a social market economy.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The 1939 report insists on a strong Red Army.

rich-first.rationale: The doctrine opposes unequal enrichment, though Stalin accepted wage differentials.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: The USSR allied with Britain and the US in 1941.

property-franchise.rationale: Soviet doctrine disenfranchised former exploiters but not by property; universal franchise.

reification.rationale: Marxist theory of fetishism, but not discussed in the Stalin-era sources.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Marxist-Leninist argument that bourgeois freedoms are formal.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Not addressed; Soviet practice mixed laws and decrees.

racial-franchise.rationale: The Soviet system rejects racial limits on citizenship.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: The secular state did not restrict marriage by religion.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: The state was indifferent to doctrine, atheistic.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Soviet law proclaimed equality of spouses.

rent-control.rationale: State-set rents in the Soviet system.

abolish-ip.rationale: Soviet system had inventors' certificates; not abolished.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Pioneers and Komsomol organized youth under the party for service to the state.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Inferred from the sovereign state doctrine and anti-encirclement.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Stalin's 1941 speech condemns Nazi crimes against peoples.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Abolition of money and wages belongs to the eventual communist stage; under Stalin-era socialism wages persisted, so the answer is long-run only.

conscription.rationale: Stalin's 1941 speech mobilizes the whole population for the war and the Red Army rested on universal conscription.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Not addressed; social benefits were tied to Soviet citizenship and employment in practice.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Socialism distributes by work and the duty to work was constitutional, so able-bodied adults are expected to work.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Stalin's 1939 report presents the party and leadership as a purified body that clears its ranks of dross; the elite is not framed as corrupt.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Socialism in one country holds that real independence rests on a transformed economy, as the 1939 report presents Soviet industrial strength.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: The multinational Soviet people was not defined by ethnic nationality, though the 1939 annexations were justified by Ukrainians and Belarusians in Poland.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Anti-colonial doctrine, and the early Soviet state repudiated Tsarist treaties; not discussed in the sources read.

elective-rulers.rationale: The soviet system claims election of rulers, though in practice by party slate.

minority-veto.rationale: Democratic centralism binds minorities to decisions; the 1939 report praises party discipline.

parliament-supreme.rationale: The Supreme Soviet was nominally supreme, but real authority lay with the party; inferred.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Not addressed in any source; no basis for placing it.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Not addressed in any source; no basis for placing it.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: The privileged classes were abolished, so a paternal duty of the rich is not part of the doctrine.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Stalin calls on every citizen to join the war effort; political withdrawal contradicts active duty to the state.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Marxist critique of bourgeois culture would agree, but Soviet mass culture served the state, so adherents are split.

native-born-offices.rationale: Not addressed; the friendship of peoples line made office open to all Soviet citizens, but party loyalty mattered more.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Soviet policy recovered lost Tsarist-era lands in 1939-40, inferred from practice rather than stated doctrine.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Stalin frames the war as a patriotic war of liberation against fascist enslavers; anti-fascism is a founding value for the Soviet state.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Stalin presents Hitlerite Germany as the criminal enemy; equating communism with it would be rejected.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Marxist class analysis treats slavery as central; inferred, not discussed in the sources.

military-guardian-role.rationale: The Red Army was subordinate to the party, but guardian duties in defence of the state were praised.

paid-care-work.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; socialization of care was the Soviet line rather than wages for housework.

filial-duty.rationale: Not addressed; Stalin-era family policy stressed family obligation.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Stalin-era law from 1944 made divorce harder, though earlier Soviet law allowed it; contested by period.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: The state held the means of production and foreign trade, so foreign ownership of strategic firms is excluded.

recallable-delegates.rationale: The soviet principle of recall of delegates from Lenin, though little used under Stalin.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Land was nationalized and held by collective farms for use, which matches this principle.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: The Supreme Soviet formally approved the budget, but the party decided; split.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Land was nationalized, so foreign ownership is excluded.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: The doctrine holds that wealth in private hands gives power to exploiting classes, which socialism abolished.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Not addressed; Stalin-era law criminalized homosexuality, so inferred.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: The 1939 report explicitly keeps punitive organs and an intelligence service.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Not addressed; the Soviet state was centralist and rejected communal power-sharing.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: The state, not charity, is responsible for welfare in socialism.

term-limits.rationale: Not addressed; Stalin-era leadership had no term limits and rotation was not a doctrine.

vote-delegation.rationale: Anachronistic; not part of the soviet system, which used party-led elections.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Anachronistic; no basis in the sources.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Stalin-era socialism abolished exploitation and rewarded labour, a principle stated in the 1939 report's account of Soviet society.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Stalin's 1941 broadcast makes armed defence of the homeland a duty, with scorched earth and tribunals for those who fail it.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Stalin's 7 November 1941 speech names Russian ancestors such as Nevsky and Kutuzov as forebears of the Soviet defenders, though the Revolution is also treated as a break.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Marxism-Leninism of the Stalin era treated sex differences as natural and pushed family and motherhood policy; inferred, not discussed in the sources.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: The Soviet line held the 'woman question' solved in socialism, so no separate political category for women was wanted; inferred.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: The wartime appeals to ancestors and the fallen made heroes objects of public reverence, though sacred language sat uneasily with state atheism; inferred.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Soviet patriotism rested on materialist Marxism-Leninism, which reads politics as class interests, though the 1941 speeches use moral language of good and evil; inferred.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: The Soviet Union saw itself as the homeland of socialism meant to hold its peoples, so a homeland acting only as a diaspora centre runs against it; inferred.

culture-before-state.rationale: The party and the strong socialist state led culture and everything else, so cultural renewal first is inferred to be rejected.

god-not-male.rationale: The state was atheist, though it allied with the Church in the war; neither side of this question was a doctrine.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: The state held women formally equal but treated religious texts as outside its authority, so the statement's standard was not a position; inferred as split.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: The friendship of peoples doctrine opposed economic life tied to one group, and the economy was state-owned, though Russians were called the leading people.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: The Soviet system organised republics around nationalities yet also split and deported peoples; the sources show both, so it is inferred as split.

independent-unions.rationale: Inferred from Stalin-era practice, where unions were run under party leadership as transmission belts; the speeches do not discuss unions.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Stalin's 1939 report presents the Soviet state as a state of workers and peasants led by the party, though power was exercised by the party.

local-essentials-public.rationale: A planned socialist economy with public ownership of the economy is basic to the doctrine, so local utilities stay public.

second-chamber.rationale: Inferred from the Soviet legislature's two chambers including a Soviet of Nationalities; the sources do not discuss it.

municipal-property.rationale: Ownership was by the state and collective farms, not by local communities.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Soviet patriotism rests on a centralised party-state, not on towns whose assemblies decide.

family-wage.rationale: Inferred from Soviet pro-family and pro-worker policy; sources do not discuss wages.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Unaddressed in the sources; adherents' view cannot be inferred.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Inferred from the party-state's surveillance and control; sources do not discuss payments.

online-anonymity.rationale: Inferred from the party-state's surveillance and control; sources do not discuss online life.

person-over-state.rationale: The doctrine asks sacrifice for the homeland and state (see 1941 broadcast); inferred.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Inferred from Marxist-Leninist materialism; Stalin's 1941 and 1945 speeches do not take a stance on spiritual nature.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: The Soviet state was centralised and the national republics' rights depended on the centre; inferred.

gm-crops.rationale: Unaddressed in the sources; Stalin-era agriculture and genetics make adherents' view uncertain.

dense-cities.rationale: Inferred from Stalin-era industrialisation and urbanisation, which the 1939 report celebrates.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Soviet patriotism rests on the friendship of the peoples and rejects racial theory.

racial-pride.rationale: Stalin's speeches invoke pride in Russian ancestors and the Russian people as leading nation, though not in racial terms.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Official doctrine called Soviet policy peaceful and the war defensive (1941 broadcast), but the state also expanded in 1939-40; split.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Stalin's nationality doctrine treated language as one criterion among several (with territory and economic life) and kept distinct Soviet nations such as Ukrainians; inferred, since these sources do not define the nation.

communal-electorates.rationale: The Soviet state claimed one socialist society of equal citizens under one party, with religious bodies subordinate; separate religious electorates contradict this.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Stalin's 1939 report describes the USSR as encircled by hostile capitalist states, and his 1941 broadcast says the enemy aims to seize Soviet lands.

free-public-college.rationale: A socialist state claiming to serve all workers is expected to provide education as a free public service, as Soviet practice did; the sources praise the new Soviet intelligentsia.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Soviet economic management ran through planning and state directives; a tax-based environmental policy is inferred to be unlikely and is anachronistic.

future-generations.rationale: Soviet patriotism looked to a lasting socialist future and the defence of the homeland for coming generations; no environmental duty is stated, so this is inferred.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Marxist-Leninist doctrine held that women should be equal participants in production and politics; no distinct women's values were given extra weight, though this is inferred.

arms-reduction.rationale: Stalin's 1939 report calls for strengthening the army and navy against capitalist encirclement, not reducing arms.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Soviet diplomacy under Stalin used confidential negotiation and agreements; the sources never endorse open diplomacy, so this is inferred.

capital-controls.rationale: A planned socialist economy under capitalist encirclement is expected to keep state monopoly of foreign trade and control of capital movement.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Stalin's 1939 report treats the army, punitive organs and state as instruments the socialist state must keep strong against capitalist encirclement, leaving no room for rival armed groups.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Stalin's 3 July 1941 broadcast demands iron discipline, tribunals for deserters and defence of the fatherland as a duty, so refusing orders is treason.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Inferred: under the planned economy wages were set by the state and unions served the party, so bargaining against employers was not the model.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Inferred: the planned economy set wages and prices centrally, so tax-credit top-ups were not a Soviet instrument.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Inferred: a planned economy financed by the state and central bank would not accept legal limits on borrowing.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Inferred from the 1939 report's picture of a hostile capitalist world order and Soviet support for peoples resisting it.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Stalin's 1939 report argued that the Soviet state must be strengthened, not wither away, even under communism while encirclement lasts.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Soviet patriotism rests on a single planned socialist economy under party direction, the opposite of leaving communities to try different systems.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Inferred: Soviet doctrine treated nature as a resource for planned production, not as capital priced in a market.

sacred-nation.rationale: Stalin's 1941 speeches invoke Russian ancestors and the fatherland as a lasting community worth any sacrifice, though in secular socialist terms.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Inferred: with free state education and no student loans, the question did not arise, but a state paying for schooling fits the doctrine.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Official doctrine held that the friendship of peoples had ended exploitation among Soviet nations and dismissed claims of one region exploiting another.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Inferred: the Marxist aim of remaking people into new Soviet citizens conflicts with a fixed human nature that should not be redesigned.

public-service-media.rationale: Soviet media were party-led instruments of the state; Stalin's speeches treat the press and information as tools of party and government.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Marxist-Leninist atheism treated religions as false, and the wartime Church alliance was tactical; inferred.

farm-price-support.rationale: Collective farms and state procurement fit state protection of farmers, though sources do not address prices; inferred.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Inferred from the defence of the homeland as a socialist duty and encirclement thinking; the Soviet bomb came late in the period.

workers-own-party.rationale: The CPSU(B) was presented as the party of the working class and its leadership was central to the doctrine.

ban-fgm.rationale: Inferred from the Soviet state's modernising and anti-custom stance toward women; sources silent.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Inferred from the official legal equality of women in the Soviet state; sources silent.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Soviet nationality policy treated each nation's language as its own, as with Moldovan; inferred.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: A planned economy under state direction leaves pollution to central rules, not private suits; inferred.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: The state rested on the party and soviets, with no formal chiefs' role; inferred.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: The era was productivist and put collective goals over liberty, but not for the environment; no position can be inferred.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Inferred from Stalin's emphasis on discipline and harsh tribunals.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Russian was promoted as the leading language of the Soviet peoples; a requirement is inferred.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Inferred from Soviet unions acting as state-led organs with near-universal membership under party leadership.

voter-id.rationale: Inferred: the Soviet system claimed universal suffrage and no citizenship-ID barrier to voting was part of its doctrine.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Inferred from the Stalin-era state, which was officially atheist yet in 1943 gave the Russian Orthodox Church a privileged place.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Inferred from the Soviet claim that real democracy is substantive and socialist, not decided by competitive elections.

premarital-sex.rationale: Inferred from the conservative turn in Stalin-era family policy that stressed marriage and family stability.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Inferred from a strong party-state that controlled information and treated order and defence of the homeland as paramount.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Inferred from a planned socialist economy with state-provided welfare, opposed to market-style cash replacement.

women-suffrage.rationale: Soviet doctrine held that women had equal political rights, including the vote and office, in the socialist state.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Inferred from the Marxist-Leninist view that religion is an instrument of reaction and women's subordination.

race-social-construct.rationale: Stalin's 1941 speeches condemned Nazi racial theory and the doctrine stressed friendship of peoples, implying races lack a scientific basis.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: The Stalin-era state had a women's department abolished in 1930 and claimed equality already achieved, so adherents are split on dedicated agencies.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Soviet socialism put land and resources under state or collective ownership, as the collective farms in Stalin's 1941 broadcast show, so first-come private ownership was rejected.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Inferred that adherents were split: the state condemned Hitlerite leaders but guarded sovereignty against capitalist encirclement.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Inferred from Marxist-Leninist atheism; Stalin's wartime alliance with the Church (s5) was tactical and did not endorse scripture's inerrancy.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Inferred from the doctrine of friendship of peoples and Soviet claims of sex equality; the sources do not discuss gender in self-rule.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Stalin's reports defend the USSR as the homeland of socialism under capitalist encirclement, and adherents would defend it regardless of criticism of its rulers.

indirect-election.rationale: Inferred as split: the soviets were organized as a pyramid, but the 1936 constitution brought direct election and the party chose the leadership; the sources do not settle it.

national-church-status.rationale: The Church was courted as an ally in the war (s5), but the Soviet state stayed secular and gave no church legal precedence; inferred.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: The friendship of peoples doctrine and the Soviet system of national republics and autonomous units gave nationalities territorial forms of self-rule, within central party control.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Inferred from centralism and a state that settled borders by force and treaty, not by local votes.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Inferred from a centralist state that guarded the inherited borders of the Russian empire and the USSR; the speeches do not discuss colonial borders.

simple-living.rationale: Inferred from Stalin's goal of industrial abundance for the Soviet people; simple living was not an ideal of the doctrine.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Inferred from Soviet practice of encouraging settlement across the republics and the Russians' leading role; restriction runs against the doctrine.

equal-conscription.rationale: Inferred from Stalin-era conscription, which was for men, with women serving as volunteers; no source states a position on equal drafting.

missingStatements.text: A multinational state should present one nation as the leading or elder among its peoples.
missingStatements.rationale: Stalin's 1945 toast calls the Russian people the leading force among the Soviet peoples, and the elder-brother image was official.
missingStatements.declined: Specific to multinational Soviet nationality policy; too narrow for the bank.

missingStatements.text: National heroes and rulers of the pre-revolutionary past should be honoured in order to inspire defence of the homeland.
missingStatements.rationale: Stalin's 7 November 1941 speech invokes Nevsky, Donskoy, Suvorov and Kutuzov as ancestors.

notes: Wikipedia says later Soviet patriotism, from Khrushchev, moved away from Russian nationalism toward a supranational Soviet people, so answers on Russian national themes would differ for that strand. The 1939 report text was read only to about 100,000 characters.
